filename: Robust Inverse Framework using Knowledge-guided Self-Supervised Learning_ An application to Hydrology.pdf
title: Robust Inverse Framework using Knowledge-guided Self-Supervised Learning: An application to Hydrology
venue: Proceedings of the 28th ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD '22)
testbed_rationale: Focuses on basin-scale streamflow and catchment attribute inverse modeling using the CAMELS benchmark, rather than atmospheric or ocean subgrid parameterization for Earth System Models.
pain_points: High measurement error, noise, and uncertainty in static catchment characteristics due to spatial and temporal heterogeneity.
Incompleteness or missing static basin characteristics, preventing model transferability across regions and continents.
Ill-posedness and high computational complexity of non-linear inverse modeling in dynamical physical systems.
High sensitivity of state-of-the-art hydrological forward ML models (like EA-LSTM) to noise in input static catchment attributes.
extraction_notes: The paper introduces Knowledge-guided Self-Supervised Learning (KGSSL) combining bidirectional LSTM encoders, self-supervised contrastive learning, sequence reconstruction, and pseudoinverse loss to infer static basin properties and improve downstream streamflow forecasting.
